mappings.rationale: Both Privacy Act Part IIIC and APRA CPS 234 para 35–36 address incident notification, but their legal triggers, regulators and timeframes are non-equivalent: CPS 234 requires APRA notification within 72 hours for material information security incidents, whereas Part IIIC requires a 30-day serious-harm assessment and notification to the OAIC and affected individuals.
mappings.equivalence_caution: CRITICAL NON-EQUIVALENCE: Notifying APRA within 72 hours under CPS 234 does NOT discharge the Privacy Act Part IIIC duty to notify the OAIC and affected individuals of an eligible data breach (nor vice versa).

mappings.equivalence_caution: CRITICAL NON-EQUIVALENCE: Prior notification to APRA under CPS 230 para 60(b) does not satisfy APP 8 cross-border personal information protection or s 16C accountability.
